title: balance.json health.win_uptime_pct is loaded and validated but never consumed by any sim code
detail: Dead tuner-facing config: a balance tuner changing win_uptime_pct sees no behavior change; the real threshold lives in .dem run setup. Violates the ODN-5 single-source intent the comment claims.
recommended_fix: Either default run surge_win_pct from balance.health.win_uptime_pct (single source), or drop the field and its validation from the catalog.

title: recharge_pct_per_tick=0 (validation-permitted) emits no-change Meter_Changed every tick and the meter can never return to 100
detail: Validation allows 0. With recharge 0 and meter<100, `h.meter_pct += 0` then emits Meter_Changed with an unchanged pct every healthy tick forever, and the "recharges when healthy" contract (header line 44) is unreachable.
recommended_fix: Validate recharge >= 1, or skip the Meter_Changed emission (and the +=0 branch) when recharge is 0.

title: A severity-0 class's Grace_Expired is silently swallowed when drain stays 0
detail: health_drain_pct_per_tick=0 is valid (only negatives reject). Such a class's expiry lands in `expired`, but with drain==0 and any_breach==true neither branch emits — Grace_Expired is dropped, contradicting the header contract "expiry while still breached emits Grace_Expired{class}".
recommended_fix: Emit the collected Grace_Expired events whenever `expired` is non-empty and the meter did not empty, independent of drain>0; or require severity >= 1.

title: Tautological assertion in test_health_hysteresis_band_and_enter pins nothing
evidence:
testing.expectf(t, s.health.grace[0].grace_left > 0 || s.health.grace[0].grace_left == 0,
		"grace cell present for email")
detail: `x > 0 || x == 0` is true for every u32, so the expectf can never fail — the "durable contract" test asserts nothing about the grace cell.
recommended_fix: Replace with a real pin, e.g. `grace_left` equals the class's catalog grace minus ticks-breached, or at minimum a bare `> 0`.

title: balance.json health block uses truncating jint while the same story's packet_types health fields use rejecting jint_strict
evidence:
core/catalog.odin:714:
			b.health.window_ticks = jint(hobj, "window_ticks", -1)

core/catalog.odin:928:
		case json.Float:   return i32(x)

core/catalog.odin:425:
			hg, okhg := jint_strict(eo, "health_grace_ticks", 0)
detail: jint silently truncates decimals, so balance.json `"drain_cap_pct_per_tick": 2.5` loads as 2 with no error, while packet_types.json decimals reject — inconsistent with the 4.3 strict-int bar the diff's own comments claim.
recommended_fix: Use jint_strict for the health block (missing-key still yields the -1 default, since jint_strict returns (def, true) when absent).

title: test_health_drain_max_not_sum_e16 comments contradict the fixture's actual grace values
evidence:
core/health_test.odin:119-120:
health_catalog_fast_grace :: proc(cat: ^Catalogs) {
	cat.packet_types[0].health_grace_ticks = 300
}

core/health_test.odin:397:
	health_catalog_fast_grace(cat) // both classes' grace 50 (the streaming

core/health_test.odin:407:
	step_n(&s, 410, cat) // streaming drains from ~405; email (grace 10) from ~100
detail: The fixture sets email's grace to 300 (streaming stays 400), but the comments claim "both classes' grace 50" and "email (grace 10)" — misdescribing the E16 assertion window in a durable-contract test.
recommended_fix: Correct the comments to the actual 300/400 graces and the real drain-start ticks (~390/~405).

title: health_update divides by window_ticks with no zero-guard; safety rests solely on catalogs_load validation
evidence:
core/health.odin:215:
		slot := int(c) * int(h.window_ticks) + int(tick % win)

core/health.odin:185:
	win := u64(h.window_ticks)

core/determinism_test.odin:63-64:
	// 4.3: the Network Health numbers (mirrors data/balance.json `health`) —
	// the window must be non-zero or every tick's ring index divides by zero.
detail: The only protection is load-time validation (window 1..10000); a hand-built Catalogs fixture (the established test convention) with window 0 traps on `tick % win`. The file guards beyond-catalog rows defensively but not this.
recommended_fix: Add a zero-window guard in health_update/health_ensure (return without measuring, like the n==0 E24 return).
